claims.text: The starting alloy is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The starting alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
The starting alloy has a uniform as-processed microstructure.
Ti atoms induce slight lattice distortions in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Ti-induced lattice distortions reduce lattice friction.
Reduced lattice friction lowers the critical shear stress required for dislocation motion.
Substitutional Ti-induced local distortions lower the barrier to dislocation nucleation.
Substitutional Ti-induced local distortions lower the barrier to dislocation propagation.
Facilitated dislocation motion causes lower hardness and strength.
The alloy retains high plasticity despite its low hardness and strength.
The alloy retains favorable machinability despite its low hardness and strength.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi will have lower hardness than samples with slightly modified Ti content.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi will have lower strength than samples with slightly modified Ti content.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi will show easier slip-system activation than samples with slightly modified Ti content.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi will show more active and mobile dislocation processes than samples with slightly modified Ti content.
Slightly modifying Ti content will increase lattice resistance relative to the equimolar alloy.
The proposed mechanism applies only near the equimolar composition under ambient-temperature, quasi-static loading without secondary-phase formation.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says Ti-induced distortion lowers lattice friction, but the intervention varies Ti in either direction and predicts that any deviation from equimolar Ti will increase lattice resistance. Increasing Ti could instead be expected to increase the proposed Ti-induced friction-lowering effect; no directional or nonmonotonic dependence is supplied to resolve this.

The initial state is described as uniform, while minor local segregation is also proposed as a possible mediator. These statements may be compatible at different length scales, but the relevant meaning and scale of microstructural uniformity are not defined.
